answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a deposit that grows with the work it claims, so a flood of fake identities faces a real cost per copy. Honest work earns a slow, compounding score, like a lantern lit once and kept burning, while a fresh clone starts dark. When one identity misbehaves, the penalty ripples across every credential it shares - its onyx-stamped history, its stake, its endorsements - so splitting into many selves multiplies the loss instead of hiding it.
